Przyrow Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Przyrów, Poland

Not demolished. Jews are first recorded in Przyrów in 1789, numbering 102 by 1808 and growing to 954 by 1858; a synagogue was established no later than 1838. By the 1921 census, 802 Jews (32 percent) lived in the town. In September 1942, the Germans sent Przyrów's Jews to Koniecpol, from where they were deported weeks later to Treblinka. This cemetery, probably established in the first half of the 19th century, was not marked on an 1839 topographic map, and fell into disrepair after WWII.
